name: Neutral-current measuring relay
summary: Measuring relay fed from a CT in a neutral conductor or star-point connection, responding to neutral current.
description: This relay form is used where a CT is installed in a neutral conductor or in the earthing connection of a transformer or generator star point. Current there indicates earth faults or, in four-wire systems, heavy unbalance and triplen harmonic loading, depending on where the CT sits.

The symbol identifies the measured conductor but not the purpose. A neutral CT in the star-point earth lead gives standby earth-fault protection, while one in the four-wire neutral of a feeder sees load unbalance as well, so settings and grading differ greatly.
readingNotes: Confirm whether the CT is in the neutral conductor or the earthing lead.
Check grading against downstream earth-fault devices.
distinction: A neutral-current relay measures one neutral path; a residual connection sums the three phase CTs to derive the same quantity.
